'''Christian Genest''' ({{IPAc-en|ʒ|ən|ɛ}}; born January 11, 1957, in [[Chicoutimi, Quebec]]) is a professor in the Department of Mathematics and Statistics at [[McGill University]] (Montréal, Canada), where he held a [[Canada Research Chair]] between 2011 and 2025. He is the author of numerous research papers in [[multivariate analysis]], [[nonparametric statistics]], [[extreme-value theory]], and [[multiple-criteria decision analysis]].

He is a recipient of the Statistical Society of Canada's Gold Medal for Research and was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2015.

==Contributions==

Genest is best known for developing models and statistical inference techniques for studying the dependence between variables through the concept of [[Copula (probability theory)|copula]].<ref name="RSC-2015">{{cite web | url=https://www.rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/pdf/NF%20Citations%202015_2.pdf | title=RSC Class of 2015 | access-date=August 8, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151220065528/https://www.rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/pdf/NF%20Citations%202015_2.pdf | archive-date=December 20, 2015 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He has designed, among others, various techniques for selecting, estimating and validating copula-based models through rank-based methods. His methodological contributions in [[multivariate analysis]] and [[extreme-value theory]] found numerous practical applications in finance, insurance, and hydrology.<ref>[https://rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/pdf/M%26A%202020.pdf John L. Synge Award 2020]</ref>

Throughout his career, Genest also made significant contributions to the development of techniques for the reconciliation and use of expert opinions and [[Pairwise comparison (psychology)|pairwise comparison]] methods used to establish priorities in [[multiple-criteria decision analysis]].<ref name="SSC-2011">{{cite web | url=http://www.ssc.ca/en/award-winners/award-winners-2011 | title=SSC Award Winners for 2011 | access-date=August 8, 2021 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140225184356/http://www.ssc.ca/en/award-winners/award-winners-2011 | archive-date=February 25, 2014 }}</ref> He is the author or co-author of over 380 scientific publications, about half of which appeared in peer-reviewed journals. Part of his work is also concerned with the history of statistics and scientometrics. Christian Genest has given over 360 invited talks, including 90+ presentations for a general audience.<ref name="Stat-Trek">{{cite journal | url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/demo-2016-0005/html | title="Stat Trek: An Interview With Christian Genest, by F. Durante, G. Puccetti, M. Scherer and S. Vanduffel, ''Dependence Modeling'', vol. 4 (2016), pp. 109-122" | journal=Dependence Modeling | date=12 May 2016 | volume=4 | issue=1 | doi=10.1515/demo-2016-0005 | access-date=August 8, 2021| last1=Durante | first1=Fabrizio | last2=Puccetti | first2=Giovanni | last3=Scherer | first3=Matthias | last4=Vanduffel | first4=Steven | s2cid=147717691 | hdl=2434/391032 | hdl-access=free }}</ref>

==Birthplace and education==

Christian Genest was born on January 11, 1957, in [[Chicoutimi]] (Québec, Canada). He was trained as a mathematician at the [[Université du Québec à Chicoutimi]] (B.Sp.Sc., 1977) and at the [[Université de Montréal]] (M.Sc., 1978) before completing graduate studies in statistics at the [[University of British Columbia]] (Ph.D., 1983). His thesis, entitled "Towards a Consensus of Opinion",<ref name = "genealogy">{{Cite web|url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=17625|title=Christian Genest at Mathematics Genealogy Project|work=Mathematics Genealogy Project|access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> was written under the supervision of James V. Zidek and earned him the Pierre Robillard Award from the Statistical Society of Canada (SSC) in 1984.<ref name="Pierre Robillard Award">{{cite web | url=http://www.ssc.ca/en/award-winners#Pierre | title=Pierre-Robillard Award winners|access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref>

==Academic career==

After completing his PhD, Christian Genest was a postdoctoral fellow and visiting assistant professor at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] (Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania) in 1983–84. From 1984 to 1987, he was an assistant professor in the Department of Statistics and Actuarial Science at the [[University of Waterloo]] (Waterloo, ON). He was then hired by [[Université Laval]] (Québec, QC), where he was promoted to the ranks of associate in 1989 and professor in 1993. He joined [[McGill University]] (Montréal, QC) in 2010, where he held a Canada Research Chair in Stochastic Dependence Modeling from 2011 to 2025.<ref name="CRC">{{cite web | url=http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=2847 | title=Canada Research Chair | date=29 November 2012 |access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref>

Christian Genest was the first recipient of the CRM-SSC Prize in 1999.<ref name="CRM-SSC">{{cite web | url=http://www.ssc.ca/en/award-winners#CRM_SSC | title=CRM-SSC Award winners |access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> He received the SUMMA Research Award from [[Université Laval]] the same year.<ref name="SUMMA">{{cite web | url=http://www.scom.ulaval.ca/Au.fil.des.evenements/1999/06.10/genest.html | title=Le Fil des Événements, June 10, 1999 | access-date=August 8, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170720/http://www.scom.ulaval.ca/Au.fil.des.evenements/1999/06.10/genest.html | archive-date=March 3, 2016 | url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2011, the [[Statistical Society of Canada]] awarded him its most prestigious distinction, the gold medal, "in recognition of his remarkable contributions to multivariate analysis and nonparametric statistics, notably through the development of models and methods of inference for studying stochastic dependence, synthesizing expert judgments and multi-criteria decision making, as well as for his applications thereof in various fields such as insurance, finance, and hydrology."<ref name="SSC-2011">{{cite web | url=http://www.ssc.ca/en/award-winners/award-winners-2011 | title=SSC Award Winners for 2011 | access-date=August 8, 2021 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140225184356/http://www.ssc.ca/en/award-winners/award-winners-2011 | archive-date=February 25, 2014 }}</ref> Christian Genest is a fellow of the [[American Statistical Association]] since 1996,<ref name="ASA Fellows">{{cite web | url=https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx | title=ASA Fellows | access-date=April 24, 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425013824/https://www.amstat.org/ASA/Your-Career/Awards/ASA-Fellows-list.aspx | archive-date=April 25, 2019 | url-status = dead }}</ref> a fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]<ref name="IMS Fellows">{{cite web | url=https://www.imstat.org/honored-ims-fellows/ | title=IMS Fellows|access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> since 1997, and an honorary member of the [[ASSQ (Statistics)|Association des statisticiennes et statisticiens du Québec]] since 2012.<ref name="Liaison">{{cite web | url=http://www.ssc.ca/webfm_send/1002 | title=Liaison, vol. 26, no. 3, p. 48 | access-date=February 14, 2014 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140225185241/http://www.ssc.ca/webfm_send/1002 | archive-date=February 25, 2014 }}</ref>
He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Canada]] in 2015<ref name="RSC-2015">{{cite web | url=https://www.rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/pdf/NF%20Citations%202015_2.pdf | title=RSC Class of 2015 | access-date=August 8, 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151220065528/https://www.rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/pdf/NF%20Citations%202015_2.pdf | archive-date=December 20, 2015 | url-status = dead }}</ref> and received a Humboldt Research Prize from the  [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] in  2019.<ref name="Humboldt-2019">{{cite web | url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_auswahlergebnisse.main | title=List of award winners since March 2013 (in German or English) | access-date=January 28, 2020 | archive-date=August 20, 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190820035258/http://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_auswahlergebnisse.main | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was the first statistician to receive the [[John L. Synge Award]] in 2020<ref>[https://rsc-src.ca/sites/default/files/pdf/M%26A%202020.pdf John L. Synge Award 2020]</ref> and the [[CRM-Fields-PIMS prize]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.fields.utoronto.ca/news/Christian-Genest-awarded-2023-CRM-Fields-PIMS-Prize | title = Christian Genest awarded the 2023 CRM-Fields-PIMS Prize | website = [[The Fields Institute]] | date = January 19, 2023 | location = Toronto | access-date = January 30, 2023}}</ref> In 2024, he was awarded the [[Parzen Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christian Genest: Recipient of the Emanuel and Carol Parzen Prize for Statistical Innovation 2024 |url=https://ssc.ca/en/publications/ssc-liaison/vol-38-7-2024-12/christian-genest-recipient-emanuel-and-carol-parzen-prize |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=ssc.ca}}</ref>

==Community service==

Christian Genest has served the mathematical and statistical communities in many ways. Among others, he was director of the ''Institut des sciences mathématiques du Québec'' (2012–15), president of the [[Statistical Society of Canada]] (2007–08)<ref name="SSC Board of Directors">{{cite web | url=http://www.ssc.ca/en/about/history-ssc/historical-list-of-the-board-of-directors | title=SSC Board of Directors Historical List |access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> and president of the [[ASSQ (Statistics)|Association des statisticiennes et statisticiens du Québec]] (2005–08). He served on [[Statistics Canada]]'s Advisory Committee on Statistical Methods for several years, and on the editorial board of various peer-review journals, including ''[[The Canadian Journal of Statistics]]'' (1988–2003), the ''Journal de la Société française de statistique'' (1999–2008) and the ''[[Journal of Multivariate Analysis]]'' (2003–2015).<ref name="JMVA Editorial Board">{{cite web | url=http://www.journals.elsevier.com/journal-of-multivariate-analysis/editorial-board/ | title=JMVA Editorial Board |access-date=February 14, 2014}}</ref> He was also editor in chief of ''The Canadian Journal of Statistics'' (1998–2000) and guest editor for various books and special issues, including two for ''Insurance: Mathematics and Economics'' (2005, 2009). From September 2015 to May 2019, he was editor in chief of the ''Journal of Multivariate Analysis''. His many contributions earned him the Distinguished Service Award from the [[Statistical Society of Canada]] as early as 1997.<ref name="SSC Distinguished Service Award">{{cite web | url=http://www.ssc.ca/en/award-winners#Service | title=SSC Distinguished Service Award winners|access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref>

==Others==

Christian Genest is married to [[Johanna G. Nešlehová]], professor of statistics at McGill University.<ref name="Johanna Nešlehová">{{cite web | url=http://www.math.mcgill.ca/neslehova/ | title=Johanna Nešlehová |access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> One of his sisters, Sylvie Genest, is a professor in the Faculty of Arts at the [[Université du Québec à Montréal]].<ref name="Sylvie Genest">{{cite web | url=https://professeurs.uqam.ca/professeur/genest.sylvie/ | title=Sylvie Genest |access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref> Christian has four children (Marianne, Arnaud, Vincent, Richard). Vincent Genest is himself a researcher and the author of many papers in mathematical physics.<ref name="Publications by Vincent">{{cite web | url=https://arxiv.org/search/?searchtype=author&query=Genest%2C+V+X | title=Publications by Vincent Genest on arXiv |access-date=August 8, 2021}}</ref>
